body: Somebody saw this [before](https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/issues/824), but I couldn't repro it. A crash dump might be helpful.

I saw this issue, I was not sure if this was the same problem. I also can't repro. The issue happens on WP, Android and Unit Tests, so it's not specific to my unit tests but it indeed makes them crash (as any other stackoverflowexception).

As I see, there is a fix for the bug you mentioned that was committed. What I can do is try the new version when it's ready and tell you if the issue is gone. I'll leave you the choice to close or leave the issue open.

Regarding crash dumps, I'm unfortunately unaware how to do them :-/

That issue was closed for different reasons. There is no fix because we don't know how it happens. If it crashes on the desktop, [here](http://blogs.msdn.com/b/debugger/archive/2009/12/30/what-is-a-dump-and-how-do-i-create-one.aspx) is how you can make a crash dump.
I should be able to make a console app that crashes on which you'll have the dump. Let me look at this and come back to you.

Okay I was not able to reproduce from a console app (it's the exact same code as the unit test, what the heck…) but looking into Visual Studio I found the « save dump as » option which allowed me to put this dump from my unit test crash.

Here it is, I hope this helps :
https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B6kaeItD7VQ_bXczOUhBOXl1TDA/view?usp=sharing
Thanks for taking the time to do this, I'll take a look and let you know.

Sure, no problem ! This is an amazing library and I'm glad to help you.

If anyone has the problem, the final workaround I am using is :
`.ForMember(target => target.MyEnumProperty, options => options.MapFrom(source => (int)source.MyEnumProperty))`

This is enough for automapper to work.

Do not hesitate to ask for more informations / dumps / code structure explanations / etc.
@jbogard The problem is with the PCL assembly. TypeExtensions.GetCustomAttributes calls itself and overflows the stack.

I saw that too, but I couldn't figure out and prove which of the builds of Automapper the recursion was happening.  In VS 2015 It looked like instead of recursion it would call Type.GetCustomAttributes() and not the extention method recursively for Automapper.Net4 solution. (The one I do all my testing on)
@PaulAchess I just pushed a potential fix, the latest on the MyGet feed will have this change.

AutoMapper **4.1.0-ci1007** (Prerelease) from the MyGet feed **has fixed the issue** on my unit tests and my projects.

Great job !
I'm not sure: should I close this issue or should I leave it for you to close it? (for instance if you want to close it when you push a version, I don't know how this all works)
Thanks everyone for the answer and for your quick fix :)

issue.title: Strange exceptions mapping enums
issue.body:
Hello. First of all awesome work

Second. I have tried to check if this issue is reported. Haven't found anything.

Then the real thing. I am creating a UWP application. I am creating most of the applications as PCLs, and will create just the presentation with UWP Project.

The problem arose when I tried to call AssertConfigurationIsValid in my Brand new UWP Project. An StackOverflowException was thrown. Which was strange, because I have like 300 tests. They are .NET tests, not UWP, that's certain.

I have tried to remove and remove code until I found the problem. And it was an enum in one of the entities. If I remove it, it Works.
I have reduced it all to a simple test solution with 3 projects:
- A pcl with an entity with a single property that is an enum
- A regular .NET class library with a XUnit test that creates a map, seals the configuration and calls AssertConfigurationIsValid. It Works.
- A regular UWP class library with a XUnit test that creates a map, seals the configuration and calls AssertConfigurationIsValid. It throws an StackOverflowException.

In both cases the code is the same:

Mapper.CreateMap<XElement, MyEntity>().ForMember(dest => dest.MyEnum, opt => opt.UseValue(MyEnum.Value1));
            Mapper.Configuration.Seal();
            Mapper.AssertConfigurationIsValid();
